title: pr-5821-add-representative-workload-runners-and-reporting-pipeline
author: Ava Martinez
description: Add representative workload runners (cpu/gpu/multi-model), profiling baselines, and a lightweight reporting pipeline for the Benchmark Lab. Motivation: teams need reproducible, production-like throughput and latency baselines and automated nightly reporting so regressions are caught early. This PR introduces: 1) workload runners: cpu_runner, gpu_runner, sequence_short/long profiles, and a multi-model fanout runner to exercise KV cache and context handling; 2) profiling baselines: baseline collectors that emit p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, memory residency, and KV cache hit rates; 3) reporting pipeline: a small ETL job that ingests JSON test outputs, aggregates baselines by model/profile/commit, stores canonical CSV artifacts, and pushes summary metrics to the existing benchmark dashboard; 4) CI integration: a dedicated perf-ci job that runs representative micro-benchmarks on a small infra pool and uploads artifacts to the reporting bucket. Checklist: - [x] Implement runners and CLI knobs for sequence length, batch size, concurrency - [x] Add baseline collectors and protobuf-lite schema for outputs - [x] Implement ETL/reporting job and dashboard ingest contract - [x] Add perf-ci job config and GitHub Actions workflow - [x] Add docs and quickstart examples for running locally and in CI Backwards compatibility: runners are additive and opt-in via the CLI flag --bench-profile; no changes to existing test harness. Related: links to Linear tasks ENG-1983 ENG-2042.
commits: feat(bench): add cpu_runner and gpu_runner with unified runner interface
feat(bench): add multi_model_fanout runner and kv-cache exercise workload
chore(bench): add baseline collector, output schema, and CSV serializer

docs(bench): add quickstart and example configs for runners and reporting
